IMPLEMENT STORY #419 (follow-up to #289): Close the 26 catchable test gaps #289's mutation baseline found (zeroize first)

You are implementing exactly one story from the tooling track (B, deterministic gates) of the code-health epic (#330) on branch story-419-mutant-gaps, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED and merged, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

RULES
- Scope: this story and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- A gate must be shown to bite: for every new check, plant the violation it exists to refuse, run the check and see it fail with the stated reason, then remove the plant. Record each removal control (what you planted, the command, the failure text) in your notes and in the commit message. A gate never seen failing is not done.
- Tests: assert exact values and exact error text, never is_err() alone.
- A gate must fail closed. Read typed data where it exists (cargo metadata, or serde over the file's own format with a dependency the workspace already has). Where you must scan text, refuse anything the scanner does not recognise rather than skipping it. Plant the evasions as removal controls: indentation, quoting, trailing comments, flow syntax, keys split across lines, multi-line groups and aliases. Two earlier gates in this track failed open because they scanned lines and skipped what they did not recognise.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new production line and branch reachable by a test.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Required status checks are branch protection and must keep their exact names: "format, clippy, contracts", "test (ubuntu-latest)", "test (macos-latest)", "exact coverage gate", "release binary artifact", "dependency licenses (cargo-deny)", "RustSec dependency audit". Prefer gates that ride those existing checks (a Rust test, clippy configuration, the cargo-deny job) over new jobs, because a new required check needs the operator to change branch protection. If you add a job, say so in notes as an operator action.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Your seat has no network. The host facts below were resolved on the host for you. Use them, and do not invent versions, hashes or checksums.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#419)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

Facts resolved on the host on 2026-09-26:
- #289 has merged (fec48437). quality/mutants/{brokkr-core,brokkr-protocol}.missed.txt are the committed allow-lists, and scripts/mutants.sh measures a scope and compares it with them. cargo-mutants 27.1.0 is installed on the host, but your seat may not be able to run it. For each gap, prove the kill the way cargo-mutants would: apply the mutation by hand, run the new test and see it fail, then restore. Record each mutation as the removal control. Then remove exactly the killed entries from the allow-lists.
- The operator ruling puts the zeroize-on-drop test (secret.rs:73) FIRST. It is security-relevant: a Secret's buffer must be zeroed when it drops. Test it through a seam that observes the buffer. Do not add unsafe code to read freed memory.
- Seven misses are uncatchable on the supported hosts; leave them in the allow-list: hands.rs:56 (two), hands.rs:678 (three, cfg(not(unix))), and secret.rs:498/499 (b64, equivalent).
- The six run_boxed/run_boxed_in misses (hands.rs:1133, :1162) are caught by brokkr-cli/tests/hands.rs. Move a focused test into brokkr-protocol if that is clean. Otherwise leave them, and say so.
- The ceilings: at most 100 lines per function, tests included; nesting 5; 7 parameters; test files may not grow past their baseline in quality/file-lines.txt, so prefer new test files at the gate's test paths over growing crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/tests.rs; no copied blocks.

THE ISSUE (#419), verbatim:

Part of the code-health epic #330, following #289. Operator ruling, 2026-09-26: fire this right after #289 merges.

#289's baseline (`quality/mutants/`, measured on `main` at 155aa5f0 with cargo-mutants 27.1.0) found **33 missed mutants**. Seven can never be caught on the supported hosts: 17–18, 26–28 and 32–33 in the table on #289. The other **26 are real test gaps**. Close them, each with a test that kills the mutant, and shrink the allow-lists to match.

## Order of work

1. **`secret.rs:73`: `Drop for Secret` is replaced by `()` and nothing notices.** Test that dropping a `Secret` zeroes its buffer. This is security-relevant.
2. **`secret.rs:161`:** the off-by-one at `MIN_VALUE_BYTES` in `validate_value`. Test exactly at the boundary.
3. **`hands.rs:1015`:** `drain_bounded` at exactly `OUTPUT_BYTES`.
4. **`hands.rs:638`, `:645`, `:652`:** `box_argv`'s `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME` and `NPM_CONFIG_CACHE` argv.
5. **`hands.rs:317`:** `git_facts` when `git rev-parse` fails.
6. **`hands.rs:1118`, `:1189`:** a signalled process's exit code (`-1`).
7. **`hands.rs:673`:** the uid/gid mapping.
8. **`secret.rs:227`:** the search offset in `scan_secret_refs`.
9. **brokkr-core:**
   - `dispatch.rs:300`, with `now == issued`;
   - `fold.rs:155`, the `OutOfPlace.cursor` text;
   - `fold.rs:384`, `consecutive_failures` after a scoped `"fail"`;
   - `policy.rs:619`, `EnumIn` on a third input name.
10. **`hands.rs:1133`, `:1162`:** the six `run_boxed`/`run_boxed_in` misses are caught by brokkr-cli's `hands` tests. Either move a test into brokkr-protocol, or make the mutation run for `hands.rs` include brokkr-cli's `hands` suite (#289's condition for gating protocol).

## Acceptance

- `scripts/mutants.sh` shows each fixed mutant caught, and the allow-lists in `quality/mutants/` shrink by exactly those entries.
- Each new test is bound by the mutant it kills. The mutant is the removal control.
- The exact coverage gate holds.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. A new function stays within
  cyclomatic complexity 15, and an existing one never grows more complex.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",

    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},

  ],
```

Commit 60b2552b on story-419-mutant-gaps (signed off, not pushed). It changes only tests and quality/mutants; no production line moves. Tests closed 25 of the 26 gaps; the 26th (secret.rs:227) is equivalent and stays in the allow-list, which needs an operator ruling.

REMOVAL CONTROLS (cargo-mutants 27.1.0 ran in the seat, --in-place, the full package suite each time, logs under .forge/mutants-*):
- core, the five targeted mutants: '5 mutants tested in 11s: 5 caught'. Each log has exactly one FAILED test, the new one: dispatch::tests::a_dispatch_verifies_at_the_instant_it_was_issued (dispatch.rs:300); fold::tests::an_out_of_place_refusal_names_the_cursor_it_met (fold.rs:155, both mutants); fold::tests::a_scoped_fail_counts_and_a_scoped_pass_resets (fold.rs:384); policy::tests::an_enum_refusal_names_its_own_vocabulary (policy.rs:619).
- protocol, 21 targeted mutants: '19 caught, 2 missed'. Failing tests per log: secret_drop::a_dropped_secret_frees_zeroes_not_its_value (secret.rs:73); hands::tests::the_rendering_labels_every_section_and_output_is_bounded_while_draining (1015, both mutants); hands::tests::a_toolchain_variable_is_set_by_its_own_bind_only (638/645/652); hands::tests::the_box_identity_is_the_engines_own (673, all four); hands_exits::a_failed_rev_parse_names_no_git_directory (317); hands_exits::a_box_killed_by_a_signal_reports_minus_one (1118, 1162 x3, 1189); hands_exits::run_boxed_returns_the_boxs_own_code (1133 x3, 1162 x3, 1189).
- The two misses: (a) secret.rs:161. It is the SHORT_VALUE_WARN_BYTES (8) check, not MIN_VALUE_BYTES as the issue says, so my first test aimed at the wrong bound. I retargeted it (7 bytes warn, exactly 8 is Ok(None)) and re-ran: '1 mutant tested in 12s: 1 caught', failing test secret::tests::a_value_exactly_at_the_warning_bound_is_accepted_quietly. (b) secret.rs:227 (`search = name_end + 2` becoming `- 2`) is equivalent. The four bytes between the offsets are name bytes [A-Z0-9_] (or the ':' before a one-letter name) and the closing '}}'. None of them can begin 'secret:', so find() returns the same index. It stays in the allow-list, and quality/mutants/README.md says why. Operator choice: accept it as equivalent, or remove the '+ 2' in a production change.

ALLOW-LISTS: brokkr-core.missed.txt is now empty; brokkr-protocol.missed.txt keeps 8 lines (hands.rs:56 x2, hands.rs:678 x3, secret.rs:227, secret.rs:498/499). The git diff shows exactly 25 lines removed. scripts/mutants.sh requires only that the file exists (known() checks -f), so an empty file is valid. I did not run scripts/mutants.sh baseline over the whole scope (protocol took 1h30 at -j6 per the README). The evidence is the targeted cargo-mutants runs above, with the same flags measure() uses. A full-scope baseline refresh is pending.

DESIGN AND ASSUMPTIONS:
- Zeroize seam (operator ruling: first). The integration binary crates/brokkr-protocol/tests/secret_drop.rs installs a #[global_allocator] that forwards to System. When the one watched buffer is deallocated, it read_volatile's up to 16 bytes before calling System.dealloc. That reads live memory, never freed memory, but it does add unsafe code (an unsafe impl GlobalAlloc) in a test file. The control: a plain Vec frees 'hunter22'; a Secret must free [0; 8].
- Item 10: I moved the tests into brokkr-protocol (the first option), as tests/hands_exits.rs. It uses stand-in bwrap/git shell scripts on a private PATH under the shared EnvGuard, which also serialises the tests so nothing forks while a stand-in is being written (ETXTBSY). It runs without namespaces, so it is host-independent.
- policy.rs:619 is the vocabulary-choice `if name == "strategy"` in the error text, not a third input name (EnumIn only ever carries strategy or drift_in). The test pins both exact refusal texts.
- The ids() test compares with /usr/bin/id -u/-g (absolute path, so no environment read). If the suite runs as root, the (0,0) mutant would survive; CI runners are not root.
- File ceilings: I read 'test files may not grow past baseline' as ruling 4, which bars growth only for files already over 2,000 lines. hands/tests.rs is now 1482 (baseline 1436), secret/tests.rs 513, fold/tests.rs 691, policy/tests.rs 825, dispatch/tests.rs 555, all under 2,000. adapters/tests.rs is untouched. quality/file-lines.txt is not refreshed (that needs measure.sh after coverage).

GATES RUN: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings clean; cargo test -p brokkr-core -p brokkr-protocol --locked all ok (core 79+3+9+2, protocol lib 456, hands_exits 5, secret_drop 1, doctests); git diff --check clean. PENDING: exact coverage gate (controller runs it; no production lines changed and the new files are at test paths), bundles/self compile, full-workspace test run, remote CI, full-scope scripts/mutants.sh baseline.

FOLLOW-UPS: (1) a ruling on secret.rs:227; (2) fold.rs cursor_name uses format!("{cursor:?}") in an error that is journaled, which bends ruling 3. It predates this change and I left it alone.

cargo test --workspace: 79 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Read-only; working tree left clean; no commit or fix made.

VERIFIED CORRECT (commands run in this session):
- Every claimed kill is in the cargo-mutants 27.1.0 logs under .forge/mutants-{core,protocol,161}/mutants.out/log: `grep -nE 'FAILED$|panicked at'` shows exactly the expected new failing test per mutant. core caught.txt 5/5; protocol caught.txt 19/19 plus the rerun of secret.rs:161 -> 1/1; missed.txt only secret.rs:227. The final allow-lists hold exactly the intended entries (core 0, protocol 8).
- secret.rs:73 (Drop zeroize) is killed only by the new tests/secret_drop.rs, not by the pre-existing wipe_zeroizes_the_buffer test (which calls wipe directly): the mutant log shows the lib suite green and `a_dropped_secret_frees_zeroes_not_its_value ... FAILED`. The witness reads the buffer before System.dealloc (never after free) and its plain-Vec control proves the allocator sees a non-zeroed value, so a no-op wipe cannot pass.
